lXPDttoR

QA Validation Result — 2026-08-05

Tester: QA tester on a physical Oculus/Meta Quest (2024 baseline)
Target: GoThru Navigator VR, Android package com.gothru.gothrunavigatorvr, version 1.10.12; Meta XR SDK 68.0.1; Oculus XR plug-in 4.5.1
Verdict: FAIL — confirmed coding defect

Scope and evidence boundary

The developer description contains only an image and the identifier lXPDttoR. The real-device tester validated the prepared download/resume scenarios on a Quest headset using real tour data. All normal download, pause, reopen, resume, completion, offline playback, and network-recovery scenarios passed. The single failure below was reproduced specifically after closing an in-progress download and selecting Cancel.

Validation summary

ID Scenario Method Expected result Actual result Status
VR-125-01 Start a real-tour download Black box Progress bar advances while panorama data downloads Works Pass
VR-125-02 Pause then reopen and resume a partial download Black box / gray-box trace Download resumes and progress UI advances Works Pass
VR-125-03 Complete download and use tour offline Black box Completed tour is available and navigable offline Works Pass
VR-125-04 Interrupt connectivity during download and recover Black box Download does not falsely complete and can continue after recovery Works Pass
VR-125-05 While downloading, choose Close, then Cancel; select Resume Black box / gray-box trace Resume immediately restarts the download and its progress bar updates Download does not progress automatically. Tester must repeat Close > Yes, then Resume before the bar advances. Fail

Confirmed coding finding

Severity Area Real-device evidence Code-review evidence Developer action
Major Download Tour progress/resume lifecycle after Close > Cancel The normal download flow passes, but after Close > Cancel the first Resume leaves the progress bar inactive. Repeating Close > Yes > Resume makes it run again. OnDisable() always calls Pause() then resets barProgress.fillAmount to 0; Pause() calls StopAllCoroutines(). Resume() starts one DownloadPano(currentPanoId) coroutine, but the close/cancel lifecycle does not restore the cancelled progress operation/UI state deterministically. Preserve or rebuild the in-flight download state when the close/cancel path returns to the process UI. A single Resume must continue downloading and drive the bar without a second close/confirmation cycle. Add a regression test for this exact lifecycle.

Code review

File / method Reviewed behavior Result
Assets/Source/Src/Script/UI/MainMenu/Download tour/DownloadTours.cs, OpenCloseUI() In-progress close opens the confirmation UI and calls Pause() Relevant to failed lifecycle
Same file, Pause() Hides pause, shows resume, and stops all coroutines Relevant to failed lifecycle
Same file, OnDisable() Calls Pause() and resets progress fill to zero Relevant to failed lifecycle
Same file, Resume() Restarts from currentPanoId only Does not reliably recover the Close > Cancel lifecycle in device test
Same file, normal download/completion path Download, resume, completion, offline playback, and network recovery Passed on physical device

Method coverage and confusion matrix

Method Coverage Outcome
Black box Real download, pause/resume, completion, offline playback, network recovery, Close > Cancel > Resume Four flows pass; close/cancel first-resume flow fails
Gray box Device observation traced against coroutine and UI-state lifecycle Confirms the failing behavior is consistent with the close/pause/reset implementation
White box OpenCloseUI, Pause, OnDisable, Resume, DownloadPano One lifecycle defect confirmed
Actual flow / expected classification First Resume progresses First Resume does not progress
Normal pause/reopen/resume True positive: 1 —
Close > Cancel > Resume — False negative: 1

The matrix classifies the resume/progress decision only; it is not a performance metric.

Reproduction steps — Oculus/Meta Quest 2024

  1. On stable Wi-Fi, open a real tour with multiple panoramas and choose Tools > Download Tour.
  2. Start downloading and wait until the progress bar visibly advances.
  3. Choose Close while the download is active, then choose Cancel in the confirmation dialog.
  4. Select Resume once.
  5. Observe that the download/progress bar does not automatically advance.
  6. Choose Close > Yes, then select Resume again. The progress bar advances; this confirms the workaround and reproduction.

QA conclusion

FixingDownloadToursIssue125.mp4

Only the Close > Cancel > Resume progress-lifecycle failure is reported as a developer coding bug. The other real-device validation scenarios passed. Keep Bug and Sanity Testing labels until the fix has been retested on the same headset flow.

Evidence note

The tester's recording does not show the arrow because the recorded head framing did not tilt downward. During physical headset use, the arrow was visible by glancing down without lowering the head. This is a recording-framing limitation, not a product failure.

The arrow is correctly positioned below the centre view, closer to the foreground, comfortable to access, and passes real-device validation. No coding bug is reported.
